check: verify the strict-offline entry, the last unchecked item, and whether its wording is precise
theEntrySays: Run the same two clean builds that tools/Test-S5Release.ps1 performs but with the network genuinely unavailable: the script already passes --offline --dependency-verification=strict, so the open question is only whether the local caches suffice without the network access the session currently has.

whatTheEvidenceShows.aPriorStrictOfflineBuildSucceeded: docs/evidence/s0-01/metadata-repair/offline-build-strict-rerun.txt records BUILD SUCCESSFUL in 30s with 18 tasks executed rather than up-to-date, including compileJava, test, runGameTest and remapJar.
whatTheEvidenceShows.thatRunWasUnderAnAuthorizedProxy: proxy-probe.init.gradle pins the Gradle JVM proxy to 127.0.0.1:7897 and throws if it is anything else, and proxy-connectivity.json records a HEAD request to the fabric-loom pom returning 200 through it. The setup was deliberate and approved rather than incidental, and the audit records the proxy settings as present.
whatTheEvidenceShows.theMetadataWasLockedDown: metadata-repair-audit.json records VerifyMetadata true, a count of retained POMs, modules and jars, and an explicit count of extra jars that were downloaded and then rolled back - so the lock was tightened rather than loosened.

isTheWordingPrecise.theDistinctionThatMatters: The entry asks for the network to be genuinely unavailable. What it needs is for the build to be unable to fetch anything.
isTheWordingPrecise.areTheyEquivalent: For that question, yes. --offline makes Gradle refuse the network and fail rather than silently fetch, and --dependency-verification=strict refuses any artifact whose checksum does not match the lock. Together they close both routes.
isTheWordingPrecise.whereTheyDiffer: Genuine disconnection is an environmental guarantee that cannot be bypassed; --offline is a promise the build makes to itself. For a third party re-running the check, pulling the cable is stronger evidence.
isTheWordingPrecise.soTheEntryIsRightToAsk: It is asking for the stronger form, which is appropriate for a release prerequisite even though the weaker form has already passed.

whatIsActuallyAlreadyProven: That the local caches suffice for a full build including compileJava, test, runGameTest and remapJar - proven on 2026-09-29 by a run that executed all 18 tasks with --offline and strict verification.
whatRemainsUnproven: That the same holds for the current source, since that run predates the corridorHalfWidth change and everything this session. Test-S5Release.ps1 will re-exercise it at current source, under the same flags, which is why the entry stays open rather than closed.
headline: The entry is accurate as written, and the distinction it draws is the right one to draw - though the practical difference is small because strict verification already refuses mismatched artifacts.
